value.rationale: The first discrete stability gap among natural permutation vertices of the Birkhoff polytope and the exceptional smallest order supply a complete metric classification: near-maximal exact arrangements must have a sharply controlled coincidence pattern. The distinction between unrestricted continuous volumes and vertex-supported discrete levels makes the mathematical question well posed and reusable.

final_claim: All n>=4: largest tetrahedron of arbitrary Birkhoff points has volume n^(3/2)/3, only four pairwise support-disjoint permutation vertices. Among nonmaximal vertex tetrahedra, sharp n>=5 second squared volume n(n-1)(2n+1)/18 and gap n(n+1)/18, with unique one-pair single coincidence; n=4 second volume sqrt(46)/3 and distinct two-overlap pattern.
limitations: n>=4 and Frobenius metric; unrestricted tetrahedra have no second largest volume due continuity; vertex-supported first gap only.
